text:
Ana Rodriguez: customer hit weird accounting after a streaming retry + routing fallback. provisional tokens showed up on old route and confirmed on new route -> net double provisional/confirmed for same toolcall id. anyone seen cross-route double-counting like this?

Tom Wu: hm. did the client reconnect to a different region or model?

Ana Rodriguez: yes, reconnect routed to a fallback broker because the sticky lease expired during the retry. model stayed compatible but route tag changed.

Sofia Ramirez: logs?

Ana Rodriguez: trace: tx-2026-03-21-78
```
# ledger snippet
2026-03-21T18:11:02Z TRACE tx-2026-03-21-78 session=0xa1 toolcall_id=tc-ff provisional_tokens=24 route=eu-west-1-brokerA
2026-03-21T18:11:04Z INFO reconnect session=0xa1 new_route=eu-west-1-brokerC resume_suffix=12
2026-03-21T18:11:05Z TRACE tx-2026-03-21-78 session=0xa1 toolcall_confirm toolcall_id=tc-ff confirmed_tokens=24 route=eu-west-1-brokerC
# end -> accounting shows provisional 24 on brokerA + confirmed 24 on brokerC
```

billing-bot: Alert BILL-9002: cross-route provisional + confirmed detected for toolcall tc-ff. Candidate double-bill.

Tom Wu: root cause is that provisional ownership was scoped to route instance not globally keyed by toolcall id + session. Confirm path writes confirmed to the current route ledger and doesn't clear remote provisional markers.

Sofia Ramirez: two obvious fixes: 1) make provisional ownership global by toolcall id (claim w/owner id) so reconcilers can clear old provisional on confirm, or 2) on confirm search for matching provisionals across routes and atomically reconcile. Option 1 is safer long-term.

Ana Rodriguez: agree. short term we should add a conservative reconciliation step on confirm: if confirmed_tokens == provisional_tokens and toolcall id matches, decrement provisional across other routes. must be careful with race vs real duplicates.

Tom Wu: note: we also need console visibility. Ops couldn't tell which route had provisional vs confirmed; the per-route dashboard only shows confirmed. add provisional_count and provisional_by-toolcall to route dashboard.

Sofia Ramirez: I'll add metrics: billing.provisional_global_claims{route,toolcall} gauge and billing.cross_route_reconciliations counter. Also instrument stream.fallback_reconnect_reason tag for tracing.

Ana Rodriguez: will open GH issue and attach repro harness (client reconnect + forced fallback) and test vectors. I'll include a flaky test for race window.

Tom Wu: rollout plan: deploy conservative reconcile in canary with flag billing.reconcile_cross_route=true, enable on a small set of routes, monitor billing.cross_route_reconciliations and billing.net_charge_delta.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary billing.reconcile_cross_route=true -> 2026-03-22T02:00Z.

Sofia Ramirez: docs: add a console note under "Token accounting debugging" explaining provisional vs confirmed, and a troubleshooting checklist for when provisional spikes appear during rollouts/fallbacks.

Ana Rodriguez: assigned ENG-5891, priority P1 for the short-term reconcile patch (billing + eng-platform).

Tom Wu: follow-ups: add unit test for cross-route confirm->clear behavior, and an integration test simulating route failover during mid-toolcall. Also check implications for reserved capacity billing (Dedicated).

Sofia Ramirez: flagged potential billing edge for Dedicated customers where route affinity equals customer-owned pool. We'll add an exclusion: if route belongs to a single-customer dedicated pool, reconcile requires owner-signoff.

Ana Rodriguez: thanks team. I'll post PR link in this thread when ready and paste updated metrics graph after canary. Closing for now but will update with results.
